Chapter 13

Surface Areas and Volumes

Exam weight: 6 marks (1 VSA + 1 SA-I + 1 SA-II) | Dropped: Conversion of Solid from One Shape to Another, Frustum of a Cone

Concept Notes

  • Cube: Volume = a³, TSA = 6a²  |  Cuboid: Volume = lbh, TSA = 2(lb+bh+hl)
  • Cylinder: CSA = 2πrh, TSA = 2πr(r+h), Volume = πr²h
  • Cone: slant l = √(r²+h²), CSA = πrl, TSA = πr(r+l), Volume = ⅓πr²h
  • Sphere: Volume = 4/3πr³, TSA = 4πr²  |  Hemisphere: Volume = 2/3πr³, curved SA = 2πr², TSA = 3πr²
  • For combination solids, add/subtract the relevant curved surface areas or volumes of the parts — never double-count a shared flat face that's now internal.

VSA (1 mark) — 10 Qs

  1. Find the volume of a cube of side 5cm.
  2. Find the CSA of a cylinder of radius 7cm, height 10cm. (π=22/7)
  3. Find the volume of a sphere of radius 3cm. (π=22/7)
  4. Find the TSA of a cube with edge 6cm.
  5. Find the CSA of a cone with radius 7cm, slant height 10cm. (π=22/7) (Fig. D8)
  6. Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 14cm, height 5cm. (π=22/7)
  7. Find the volume of a cone with radius 6cm, height 7cm. (π=22/7) (Fig. D8)
  8. Find the slant height of a cone with radius 3cm, height 4cm. (Fig. D8)
  9. Find the TSA of a hemisphere of radius 7cm. (π=22/7)
  10. Find the ratio of the volumes of two spheres whose radii are in the ratio 2:3.

SA-I (2 marks) — 7 Qs

  1. A cone has radius 7cm and height 24cm. Find its slant height and CSA. (π=22/7) (Fig. D8)
  2. A cylinder and a cone have equal radius and equal height. Find the ratio of their volumes.
  3. A solid is a cylinder with hemispherical ends. Total length 20cm, radius 3.5cm. Find its volume. (Fig. D3)
  4. Find the volume of a hemisphere of radius 10.5cm. (π=22/7)
  5. A cylinder has CSA 264cm² and radius 7cm. Find its height and volume.
  6. The CSA of a cone and a hemisphere of the same radius are equal. Find the ratio of the cone's height to its radius.
  7. A cylindrical pencil of radius 5mm is sharpened to a conical tip of height 8mm. Find the volume of material removed. (Fig. D9)

SA-II (3 marks) — 8 Qs

  1. A toy is a cone mounted on a hemisphere of the same radius. Diameter of base = 6cm, height of cone = 4cm. Find the total surface area. (Fig. D1)
  2. A vessel is a hollow cylinder mounted on a hollow hemisphere; diameter = 14cm, total height = 20cm. Find the inner surface area. (π=22/7) (Fig. D2)
  3. A solid is a cylinder with hemispherical ends. Total length = 104cm, radius = 7cm. Find its volume. (Fig. D3)
  4. A cone (radius 7cm, height 24cm) is carved out of a solid cylinder of the same radius and height. Find the volume of the remaining solid. (Fig. D4)
  5. A toy is a hemisphere surmounted by a cone; radius 3.5cm, total height 15.5cm. Find the volume. (Fig. D1)
  6. An iron pillar is a cylinder (radius 8cm, height 240cm) surmounted by a cone (same radius, height 15cm). Find the total surface area of 20 such pillars. (π=22/7) (Fig. D5)
  7. A wooden toy is a cylinder (radius 3.5cm, height 10cm) with a hemispherical depression carved into each end. Find the volume of wood left. (Fig. D6)
  8. A solid is a cylinder (radius 3.5cm, height 10cm) with a cone (height 4cm) attached at each end. Find its total volume. (Fig. D7)

Chapter 14

Statistics

Exam weight: 6 marks (1 SA-I + 1 LA) | No VSA for this chapter — matches exam exactly

Concept Notes

  • Median (grouped data): L + [(n/2 − CF)/f] × h, where L = lower limit of median class, CF = cumulative frequency before it, f = frequency of median class, h = class width.
  • Mode (grouped data): L + [(f1−f0)/(2f1−f0−f2)] × h, where f1 = modal class frequency, f0 = frequency before, f2 = frequency after.
  • Mean: Direct method = Σfx/Σf; Step-deviation method = a + (Σfu/Σf) × h, where u = (x−a)/h.

Chapter 15

Probability

Exam weight: 3 marks (1 VSA + 1 SA-I)

Concept Notes

  • P(Event) = (Number of favourable outcomes) / (Total number of equally likely outcomes)
  • P(E) + P(not E) = 1
  • 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 for every event E.

VSA (1 mark) — 10 Qs

  1. A die is thrown once. Find P(getting a prime number).
  2. A die is thrown once. Find P(getting a number greater than 4).
  3. Two coins are tossed together. Find P(exactly one head).
  4. A card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52. Find P(getting a king).
  5. A card is drawn from a deck of 52. Find P(getting a red face card).
  6. A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. Find P(blue).
  7. If P(E) = 0.35, find P(not E).
  8. A number is chosen from 1 to 10. Find P(multiple of 3).
  9. A die is thrown once. Find P(getting a number less than 3).
  10. Two coins are tossed together. Find P(no head).

SA-I (2 marks) — 6 Qs

  1. Cards numbered 1 to 25 are placed in a box; one is drawn at random. Find P(prime number) and P(multiple of 4).
  2. A bag contains 4 red, 5 black and 6 white balls. One ball is drawn at random. Find P(not black) and P(white or red).
  3. From a deck of 52 cards, all face cards of spades are removed. A card is drawn from the remaining cards. Find P(black card) and P(queen).
  4. Two dice are thrown together. Find P(sum = 8) and P(sum is divisible by 3).
  5. A box contains discs numbered 1 to 90. One disc is drawn at random. Find P(perfect square number) and P(number divisible by 5).
  6. Two dice are thrown together. Find P(a doublet) and P(sum is a prime number).

Chapter PDF

Logarithms

Exam weight: 4 marks (1 VSA + 1 SA-II) | No deletions

Concept Notes

  • Product law: log(ab) = log a + log b  |  Quotient law: log(a/b) = log a − log b
  • Power law: log(an) = n log a  |  log10 1 = 0, loga a = 1
  • Log/antilog tables are used to evaluate expressions with roots, powers, and products of decimals.

VSA (1 mark) — 10 Qs

  1. Find log10 1.
  2. Find log10 1000.
  3. Find log2 32.
  4. Find log5 (1/25).
  5. Evaluate: log10 2 + log10 5.
  6. Evaluate: log10 100 − log10 10.
  7. Evaluate: 2log10 5 + log10 4.
  8. Find log3 81.
  9. Find log10 0.001.
  10. Find log7 343.
